items.difficulty_reason: H2: The author shows Ind C is closed under finite limits in C^ - products via colim_k (X_k x Y_k) computed pointwise using the exchange of filtered colimits with finite limits in Set, equalizers via colim_i Ker(f_i, g_i) with the resulting equalizer diagrams - and then concludes that finite limits commute with filtered colimits in Ind C.

core_obligations: reduces the first assertion to closure of Ind C in C^ under finite limits, and further (since C -> C^ preserves small limits) to closure under finite products and equalizers

for X = colim X_k, Y = colim Y_k via prop:ind-object-morphism (i), asserts colim (X_k x Y_k) is the product and verifies it by the multline computation (colim(X_k x Y_k))(S) = colim_k(X_k(S) x Y_k(S)) = colim_k X_k(S) x colim_k Y_k(S) = X(S) x Y(S), using prop:filtered-finite-exchange

for f, g: X => Y with f_i, g_i: X_i => Y_i supplied by prop:ind-object-morphism (iii), takes Ker(f_i, g_i) in C, writes the equalizer diagram in Set for each S and i, applies colim_i and the same exchange fact to get the equalizer diagram for colim Ker(f_i, g_i), concluding it is Ker(f, g) in C^

observes that the argument shows filtered small colimits commute with finite limits in C^, and transfers this to Ind C since Ind C -> C^ generates filtered small colimits (prop:Ind-filtered-colim) and finite limits

compared.title: Topological rings have limits, formed on underlying spaces and rings
compared.statement:
\label{lemma-topological-ring-limits}
The category of topological rings has limits and limits commute
with the forgetful functors to (a) the category of topological spaces and
(b) the category of rings.
